an3.20:1.1: “Bhikkhus, possessing three factors, a shopkeeper soon attains vast and abundant wealth.
an3.20:1.3: Here, a shopkeeper has keen eyes, is responsible, and has benefactors.
an3.20:1.4: (1) “And how, bhikkhus, does a shopkeeper have keen eyes?
an3.20:1.5: Here, a shopkeeper knows of an item:
an3.20:1.6: ‘If this item is bought at such a price and sold at such a price, it will require this much capital and bring this much profit.’
an3.20:1.7: It is in this way that a shopkeeper has keen eyes.
an3.20:2.2: Here, a shopkeeper is skilled in buying and selling goods.
an3.20:2.3: It is in this way that a shopkeeper is responsible.
an3.20:3.1: (3) “And how does a shopkeeper have benefactors?
an3.20:3.2: Here, rich, wealthy, affluent householders and householders’ sons know him thus:
an3.20:3.3: ‘This good shopkeeper has keen eyes and is responsible; he is able to support his wife and children and pay us back from time to time.’
an3.20:3.4: So they deposit wealth with him, saying:
an3.20:3.5: ‘Having earned wealth with this, friend shopkeeper, support your wife and children and pay us back from time to time.’
an3.20:3.6: It is in this way that a shopkeeper has benefactors.
an3.20:3.7: “Possessing these three factors, a shopkeeper soon attains vast and abundant wealth.
an3.20:4.1: “So too, bhikkhus, possessing three qualities, a bhikkhu soon attains vast and abundant wholesome qualities.
an3.20:4.3: Here, a bhikkhu has keen eyes, is responsible, and has benefactors.
an3.20:4.4: (1) “And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu have keen eyes?
an3.20:4.5: Here, a bhikkhu understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.’
an3.20:4.6: It is in this way that a bhikkhu has keen eyes.
an3.20:5.2: Here, a bhikkhu has aroused energy for abandoning unwholesome qualities and acquiring wholesome qualities; he is strong, firm in exertion, not casting off the duty of cultivating wholesome qualities.
an3.20:5.3: It is in this way that a bhikkhu is responsible.
an3.20:6.1: (3) “And how does a bhikkhu have benefactors?
an3.20:6.2: Here, from time to time a bhikkhu approaches those bhikkhus who are learned, heirs to the heritage, experts on the Dhamma, experts on the discipline, experts on the outlines, and inquires:
an3.20:6.3: ‘How is this, Bhante? What is the meaning of this?’
an3.20:6.4: Those venerable ones then disclose to him what has not been disclosed, clear up what is obscure, and dispel his perplexity about numerous perplexing points.
an3.20:6.5: It is in this way that a bhikkhu has benefactors.
an3.20:6.6: “Possessing these three qualities, a bhikkhu soon attains vast and abundant wholesome qualities.”
